text:
Amelia: Heads up — we're seeing a sharp throughput drop in us-west-2 dedicated around 23:10 UTC. Worker processes on the pool started OOMing and then respawning in waves, which killed steady throughput. I have logs + profiles.
Diego: Any recent rollouts or kernel changes in that region? Could be a regression in selection heuristics.
Amelia: ops-bot shows a rollout earlier tonight.
infra-bot: deploy service/runtime v2.14.0 -> us-west-2 at 21:05:12 UTC by ci/cd
Raj: Ok. Can you paste the tail of the node logs and any NV/allocator errors?
Amelia: Pasting representative snippet from node-42:
```
[23:09:58] cuda: failed to allocate 268435456 bytes: out of memory
[23:09:59] worker[42]: kv_cache.growth current=1.9GB max=2.0GB
[23:09:59] worker[42]: aborting request, sending SIGTERM
[23:10:00] supervisor: respawn worker pid=4321
[23:10:03] cuda: failed to allocate 134217728 bytes: out of memory
[23:10:04] worker[42]: restart count=5
```
Chen: KV usage does look abnormal — kv items and bytes climbed steadily after the rollout. I pulled metrics from /metrics on node-42:
```
kv_items 412345
kv_total_bytes 2034123456
host_mem_used_bytes 12500000000
gpu_mem_used_bytes 9000000000
```
Chen: Also ran a quick perf collection on the canary host; top hotspots:
- cudaMalloc / cudaFree ~ 38%
- kernel-selection heuristics (runtime/selection.cpp) ~ 22%
- kv-evict/gc path ~ 12%
Diego: Kernel-selection at 22% is suspicious — that code path changed in v2.14 to prefer small-batch fastpath for sequences < 64. The goal was lower p99 latency but maybe it triggers memory allocation patterns we didn't exercise.
Raj: Could be interaction between fastpath and new batching heuristic — more prefix caching/KV pinning per request, causing fragmentation and larger allocations. Suggests we've hit a fragmentation + thundering restart loop: OOM -> restart -> cache rebuild -> alloc surge -> OOM.
ops-oncall: I can flip a rolling rollback on the affected pool if we want to revert v2.14 in us-west-2.
Amelia: We tried a quick canary tweak: reduced batch_max from 32 -> 8 on node-43. Result: OOMs stopped for that node, KV growth rate slowed, throughput per-node reduced ~12% but overall cluster throughput stabilized.
Diego: That aligns with batching heuristics amplifying allocator pressure. If batch_max was allowing large combined allocations, fragmentation spikes.
Chen: NVProf snapshot shows larger pinned memory allocations and lower reuse across requests post-rollout. Also noticed GC sweep latency spiking — evict path couldn't keep up with growth.
Raj: Immediate mitigations:
- Roll back kernel-selection fastpath (v2.14 -> previous) on affected pool
- Temporarily cap batch_max=8 for dedicted GPU pools
- Increase KV eviction aggressiveness (lower threshold) until we have a fix
Diego: I'm rolling a revert to canary now (reverting commit 9f3c7a2) and will watch for OOMs.
infra-bot: rollback service/runtime v2.14.0 -> v2.13.7 on us-west-2 canary at 23:28:01 UTC
Amelia: After rollback on canary: node-43 stabilized (no OOMs for 20m); worker restarts stopped and throughput returned to near-normal. Good signal.
Chen: Next steps for root cause:
- Bisect the selection heuristic change to find exact line causing larger allocation patterns
- Add targeted unit test for allocator pressure (simulate many small-batch workloads with varying KV hit rates)
- Improve KV eviction metrics and add an alert for sustained kv_total_bytes growth vs host_mem
- Re-run perf suites with v2.14 on larger canary fleet covering long-running cache scenarios
Raj: Also investigate whether the recent CUDA driver update we pulled in last sprint changed allocator behavior; check driver version on affected hosts.
ops-oncall: Action items assigned: Amelia (incident ticket + mitigation runbook), Diego (bisect & revert tracking), Chen (profiling deep dive + nvprof artifacts), Raj (KV eviction tunables & alerting). I'll follow up in incident ticket.
Amelia: Creating incident ticket I-2026-342 and attaching logs, nvprof, and quick canary data. For now: rollback confirmed and cluster stable. Will update when bisect has results.
Diego: Thanks — good catch. :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: Closing our immediate alert set. Will re-open if OOMs reappear.
Amelia: Closing thread here — incident ticket will hold the postmortem.
